title: Host-native C scalars and qualified aggregate layout are different concerns
summary: Foreign Runtime v0.22.6 supplies ABI-native aliases such as size_t, ssize_t, socklen_t, short and unsigned long. These make function signatures and scalar fields use their real C implementation types without weakening profile authority for aggregate offsets, sizes and padding.
invariants: Use size_t/ssize_t/socklen_t and other ABI-native C aliases where the C prototype uses those implementation types.
A host-native scalar does not make a struct layout architecture-neutral.
msghdr, cmsghdr, iovec, pollfd, ucred and stat remain profile-qualified aggregates.
Fixed-width types remain appropriate only where the ABI/kernel record truly specifies that width.
procedure: Ask whether a fact is a C scalar width or an aggregate layout/constant fact before deciding whether Foreign Runtime datatype resolution or the bridge profile owns it.

provenance.claim: Qualification defines ABI-native scalar use and explicitly preserves profile authority for aggregate layouts, with an 18-assertion forcing test.
Foreign Runtime v0.22.6 defines ABI-native C scalar aliases and distinguishes portable native scalar typing from ABI-qualified aggregate layout.
provenance.note: Dependency authority for native C scalar semantics.
